propertyTax.unit: CAD per assessed residential dollar per year
notes: Use the tax year's assessed value, not the asking or purchase price.
This is base residential tax. Actual local improvement levies, special taxes, adjustments and arrears are separate.
A multi-class property requires the appropriate assessed portion and rate for each class.

future.label: Your tax scenario
notes: The 2027–2030 budget was being developed at the verification date. No final 2027 property tax rate was verified.
Budget requests, infrastructure needs and citywide revenue changes are not an individual property's tax increase.
Keep editable municipal, provincial and assessment assumptions separate. Do not assign probabilities or call an assumption a forecast.

budgetContext.scope: overall municipal property tax revenue; not an individual combined bill change
budgetContext.notes: Final 2026 tax rates are available and should drive the estimate instead of the budget headline.

localImprovementAndSpecialTaxes.openAddressApiStatus: No free/open address-level levy API verified in this research.
localImprovementAndSpecialTaxes.label: Check your tax bill for extra levies
notes: Some properties pay local improvements such as paving or sidewalks; financing can be included.
An annual landscape/boulevard special tax can apply in participating communities; community membership alone does not establish a property's amount.
Use an actual tax bill or City Tax Certificate/Tax Information Report. Paid reports can be searched by address, roll or other property identifiers.

action.label: Find City property and tax reports

residentialMetered.applicability: Residential metered service; confirm the billing class and meter arrangement. Many condos use multi-family billing or include utilities in condo fees.

carts.applicability: City cart service recipients. Confirm service at the property; private condo waste charges may be in condo fees.

illustration.kind: computed example, not an observed household bill
illustration.label: 19 m³ over 30 days, with all three City carts

municipalUtilities.budgetPeriod: For annual budgeting, scale 30-day fixed charges by 365/30, then divide the annual amount by 12. Usage must refer to the same chosen period.

energyAction.label: Compare Alberta electricity and gas plans

municipalUtilities.avoidDoubleCounting: Only add amounts not already included in condo fees or another entered utility bill.

mortgage.defaultModel: Fixed rate, nominal annual interest compounded semiannually, monthly payments
mortgage.marketRateStatus: No live market mortgage quote supplied; rate is a user input.

formulas.renewalScenario: Recompute payment from remaining balance, remaining amortization and the user-entered renewal rate.

mortgage.formulaKind: mathematical derivation using the stated fixed-rate compounding convention
notes: The older FCAC disclosure example establishes compounding only; its illustrated rates and costs are not current quotes.
Variable mortgages may use a different contract convention. Do not apply the fixed-rate assumption without a label.
Term and amortization are different. Renewal rates are scenarios, not predictions.
Payment is principal and interest. Add taxes and other costs once, including when a lender collects them.

minimumDownPayment.defaultScope: standard purchase of an owner-occupied 1–2 unit home; eligibility and lending value still require lender confirmation

defaultInsurance.label: Estimated mortgage default insurance
defaultInsurance.basis: premium is a one-time percentage of base loan before adding the premium
defaultInsurance.homeStartEligibility: At least one qualifying first-time buyer OR a newly built home, with owner occupancy and high-ratio financing; additional product criteria apply.
notes: The simple tiers assume a traditional down-payment source. Non-traditional sources have different premiums.
Do not automatically add insurance when down payment is at least 20%; a lender may still require it.
Insured purchase price/lending value must be below $1.5 million. Standard calculator scope is 1–2 units; 3–4 unit rules differ.
This protects the lender and is separate from home insurance. Capitalize it once only if selected.

qualifyingRateReference.scope: OSFI minimum qualifying rate for new uninsured mortgages at federally regulated lenders; CMHC also publishes this rate for insured debt-service calculations.
qualifyingRateReference.note: This alone does not establish approval. OSFI does not require the test for qualifying uninsured straight-switch renewals with unchanged loan amount and amortization.

registrationEstimate.scope: Ordinary transfer and new mortgage; estimate assumes the stated land value and registered principal.
notes: A cash purchase has no new mortgage registration fee.
Registered collateral principal can differ from borrowed principal. Additional titles, instruments and exemptions can change the total.
Registration is only part of closing costs; obtain a transaction-specific legal quote.

monthlyOwnershipModel.kind: editorial cost model, using published rates where applicable and user-entered amounts elsewhere
monthlyOwnershipModel.formula: mortgagePI + baseTaxAnnual/12 + localImprovementAnnual/12 + municipalSpecialTaxAnnual/12 + condoFeesMonthly + utilitiesNotIncludedMonthly + homeInsuranceAnnual/12 + maintenanceAllowanceMonthly + HOAAnnual/12
monthlyOwnershipModel.notes: Allow confirmed not-applicable separately from unknown. Show entered assumptions and excluded costs beside a known subtotal.

cashToCloseModel.formula: downPayment + registrationEstimate + quotedLegalAndDisbursements + inspection + titleInsuranceIfApplicable + closingAdjustments + nonFinancedMortgagePremium + immediateRepairs - depositAlreadyPaid
notes: A deposit already paid is part of the down payment, not an additional purchase cost.
Keep quoted legal fees inclusive/exclusive of registration clear to avoid counting it twice.
Closing adjustments, new-home tax/rebate treatment and other contract items require the transaction quote.

buyerChecks.title: Confirm the actual tax bill
buyerChecks.prompt: Review current taxes, local improvements, special taxes, arrears and closing adjustments.

buyerChecks.title: Review title and registered interests
buyerChecks.prompt: Have the current title and relevant instruments checked for liens, caveats, easements and obligations; identify separate parking or storage titles.

buyerChecks.title: Check survey and property boundaries
buyerChecks.prompt: Review the real property report or transaction-specific alternative, encroachments and municipal compliance with the buyer's adviser.

buyerChecks.title: Inspect the building and private plumbing
buyerChecks.prompt: Check roof, structure, heating, electrical and plumbing condition with an appropriately licensed home inspector. Public water material records do not inspect interior plumbing.

buyerChecks.title: Read the condo reserve study and plan
buyerChecks.prompt: Compare the latest study, board funding plan, annual report and fund balance with major repairs coming due.

buyerChecks.title: Understand condo fees and upcoming work
buyerChecks.prompt: Review the budget, recent meeting minutes, fee changes, included utilities and maintenance responsibilities.

buyerChecks.title: Check condo special levies
buyerChecks.prompt: Request existing or proposed levies, payment dates and an estoppel certificate showing amounts owing.

buyerChecks.title: Review condo insurance and bylaws
buyerChecks.prompt: Check corporation insurance and deductibles, unit-owner coverage, rental and pet rules, and renovation restrictions.

buyerChecks.title: Consider a property environmental history report
buyerChecks.prompt: City EnviroSite reports can identify recorded historical uses and available environmental report references for the site and nearby land.

assessmentHistory.historyNote: Historical roll text may omit current leading zeros. Query both forms, normalize to the original current string and check property correspondence.
assessmentHistory.numberNote: assessed_value is text with commas. Remove separators; do not parse rolls or CPIDs as numbers.
assessmentHistory.duplicateRule: Deduplicate equal values across parcels for the same roll/year; never sum repeated assessment values. Preserve conflicting values and missing years.
